summary.headline: Radiant Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% on manpower costs, with standalone revenue up 7% on the IDBI mandate.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose about 7% YoY, driven mainly by the newly commenced IDBI Bank mandate, while the retail cash management business grew 5.5%. Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% a year ago because of gunmen costs, minimum wage hikes and southern-state licensed gunmen shortages. Consolidated PAT was Rs 52 million versus Rs 57 million, as Radiant Acemoney losses narrowed. Management is pinning margin recovery on price revisions it expects to complete in Q2, plus revenue growth and cost control.

segments.name: Standalone cash management
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% with IDBI mandate; BFSI and organised retail grew well, while railways, petroleum and e-commerce were sluggish. Management says the e-commerce logistics decline has been arrested and turned positive.

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics (RVL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 22.1 million in Q1 FY27, up 24% QoQ; management expects breakeven in the current quarter. Customers have been conservative in movements amid volatility linked to the war.

segments.name: Radiant Acemoney (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Losses narrowed QoQ after PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025 and fixed costs were cut. Network of over 20,000 BCs, 58,000+ Soundboxes deployed cumulatively, Rs 170 crore transaction volume in Q1; management targets breakeven in September and a full quarter breakeven in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Price revision: company has sought substantial cumulative price increases from banks; IBA committee formed and negotiations expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management expects it to reflect in the current quarter.
FY27 double-digit revenue growth targeted, including IDBI, from core business, points growth and direct clients.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 17%-18%, after factoring in price increases (per Q&A).
FY28: top-line growth of 12%-13% and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 19%-20%.
Acemoney: plans to deploy 50,000 Soundboxes in FY27, with 60%-70% already in order book; transaction revenues more meaningful in FY28.
Payment aggregator licence: revised application to be resubmitted by end-August or early September; licence expected by January or February 2027; business launch planned in FY28.
capex_capacity: Network of roughly 1,50,000 POS machines and 20,000 business correspondents cited as distribution base; spread across about 15,000 pin codes.
Acemoney plans 50,000 Soundbox deployments in FY27; cumulative 58,000+ deployed.
Tie-up with Hitachi for white-label ATM solutions mentioned.
Management said manpower is now deployed only for Soundbox/QR deployment and UPI white-label/fintech software work, with a technology team handling the rest.
demand_pricing: Standalone margin pressure from employee costs, driver and gunman costs, and cash executive service charges; minimum wage hikes in northern states and Karnataka; licensed gunmen shortage in southern states.
Long-tail smaller points are moving to payments banks and some banks have stopped the service; points from banks are not growing, which is limiting volume growth.
Last card-rate price revision was in 2021 per management; price revision is being negotiated through the Cash Logistics Association and IBA.

Competition: 42 banks served, only three or four players pan-India; management says it has not lost any large mandate on pricing in recent months and sees no noticeable change in competitor behaviour.
Management claims pricing is 10-20 bps for merchants versus 150-200 bps for credit card transactions.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the price hike taken so long, and what does business growth mean given core growth of only 1-2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts have annual escalations but banks have stopped adding points, so the company is shifting to direct clients (18% of revenue). Management expects double-digit growth in FY27 including IDBI, and a price revision negotiation to complete in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the core business growing below inflation excluding IDBI and RVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that non-IDBI, non-RVL growth is low, citing bank pullbacks and points moving to payments banks, and said the RVL impact is too small to matter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the big picture for Acemoney and its breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the acquisition aimed at leveraging the 20,000-BC network and recovering around Rs 30 crore of annual revenue lost to payments banks. Breakeven is targeted for September, with a full quarter in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Payment aggregator licence status?
qa_highlights.answer: Revised application is yet to be filed, to be resubmitted by end-September or early September; licence expected by January-February 2027 and business to start in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Would a buyback make sense?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would give the idea serious thought and bring it to the board at the coming meeting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected price increase, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, calling it substantial; negotiations expected to complete in Q2, effective July, September or October.

risks_watch: Price revision not concluding in Q2, which would keep standalone margin near 13.5%.
Continued bank points attrition and the long tail moving to payments banks.
Manpower cost inflation (own employee costs rising about 8%-9% a year) and gunmen shortages.
Acemoney breakeven slipping beyond September/Q3, and RBI payment aggregator licence timing (queries outstanding).
Management's own guidance has slipped repeatedly; an analyst noted six quarters without a settlement on the growth and cost levers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook, but cautious and somewhat evasive on price-revision quantum, competition and timelines. Management repeatedly deferred specifics to Q2 and to bank negotiations.

financial_highlights.change: vs 15.9% a year ago; vs 15% in Q4 FY26 (per CFO)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.1 billion as on 30 June 2026 (free cash Rs 644 million per CFO; Rs ~65 crore free cash per Q&A)

key_quotes: The drop is on account of increase in our manpower costs, specifically the cost of gunmen in certain regions and increase in minimum wages in few states affected our margins for this quarter.
So, cost is fairly in our control, and we have – management has taken conscious measures.
We will give a serious thought, Ankit, as in we have received similar feedback from the other market participants as well.
The new initiatives RVL& Acemoney are steadily improving and will start contributing positively to the bottom line in the second half of this year.
And we expect that current quarter, the remaining quarters of this year will help us reach this target of double -digit growth in the current year.

adds.what: Acemoney Soundbox deployments: 50,000 targeted in FY27 (58,000+ cumulative deployed; 60%-70% of FY27 target already in order book)
Payment aggregator licence and business launch (not a capacity addition; launch planned FY28)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 standalone revenue growth to double digits (10-12% midpoint 11%), backed by the IDBI mandate and price revisions, though Q1 standalone growth was only 7% and core retail grew 5.5%; the only quantified capacity addition is the 50,000 Acemoney Soundbox target, with no capex, utilisation or plant figures disclosed.
